opportunities.title: Cold-chain watchdog for the deli cases, kitchen cooling line and smoked-fish cooler
opportunities.problem: A single-location market running a full-service deli, an in-house prepared-food kitchen, on-premises bakery and smoked-fish/herring/caviar case has a lot of product sitting between 34 and 41 F, and the only record of it is whatever a staff member writes on a clipboard. NJ requires potentially hazardous food held at 41 F or less and evidences cooling as two sequential deadlines (135 to 70 F within 2 hours, then 70 F to refrigeration within a further 4 hours), which cannot be proved after the fact without timestamped readings. The store is open 9-8 seven days a week, so any overnight compressor failure or propped walk-in door runs unattended for up to 11 hours before anyone sees it, and repacked pickup and delivery orders raise the number of units in play at peak (Thanksgiving/holiday pre-orders).
evidence: FDA observed 397 retail deli departments in 2015-2016: 70.0% were out of compliance on 'foods requiring refrigeration are held at proper temperature' and 91.2% were out of compliance on the improper holding/time-and-temperature risk factor overall - the base rate for this exact department type: https://www.fda.gov/media/148247/download

NJ sets refrigeration temperature at 41 F or less and its cooling rule is cumulative and two-stage, so compliance depends on timestamped readings: https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/new-jersey/N-J-A-C-8-24-3-5

US supermarket loss averaged 11.4% for fresh fruit, 9.7% for fresh vegetables and 4.5% for fresh meat, poultry and seafood before any equipment failure, so a cooling event stacks on top of an already thin fresh margin: https://ers.usda.gov/sites/default/files/_laserfiche/publications/44306/10894_eib44_reportsummary.pdf

The store operates a deli, in-house prepared foods, bread baked on premises, European dairy/farmer cheese and a smoked fish and caviar section, i.e. 4+ separate refrigerated environments plus a kitchen cooling step: https://emporiumfoods.com/
Open Monday-Sunday 9:00am-8:00pm with holiday closures tracked separately and no stated after-hours coverage, so overnight and early-morning excursions are unwatched: https://emporiumfoods.com/faq

Holiday peaks are explicitly planned for (Thanksgiving turkey and holiday catering banners, 14-item seasonal pre-order catalog with pickup windows), which is exactly when cases get over-packed and doors get propped: https://emporiumfoods.com/shop
opportunities.agent_design: Per refrigerated unit, three independent signals rather than one, following the verified avenue design: (1) a product-simulating probe in a glycol bottle or buffered simulant, freezer-rated, mounted in the warmest spot of the case or walk-in; (2) a magnetic reed door contact, which both catches a door left ajar and suppresses nuisance alarms during stocking; (3) power/compressor state from a current clamp or a UPS-backed gateway, so a power loss is still reported when the sensor itself is dead. Sensors publish over MQTT to a gateway feeding a local database that keeps an immutable series (so the log survives an internet outage), and a deterministic rules engine fires on persistence (product temp above 41 F for more than 30 minutes), degree-minute accumulation, door-ajar duration and the NJ two-stage cooling curve. Escalation is tiered: first alert to a named on-call manager by SMS/phone, second to the owner, and a passive escalation list to the refrigeration contractor - a person always decides what to do, and no equipment is ever actuated by the agent. Daily output is an inspection-ready log PDF plus a cooling report (time from 135 F to 70 F, then to refrigeration); weekly output is a one-page digest of excursions and repeated door-ajar patterns by shift and by unit. Scope note: this is an operations/food-safety purpose (temperature and equipment state), not security, theft or intrusion surveillance, so it is not an alarm-business install under N.J.S.A. 45:5A-2. If any camera is added later to see door state, it ships video-only with the microphone hardware disabled or absent (NJ one-party consent makes audio a liability), signage and a written staff notice go up before switch-on, clips are reviewed by a person only, and anything that edges toward security, theft or intrusion is installed by a licensed alarm or electrical contractor.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A generic monitoring subscription or a $20 hobby build measures the wrong thing. Air temperature swings on every door open and every defrost cycle, so it produces either constant false alarms or washy data the staff stop trusting within a week; the value sits in product-simulating probes, per-unit threshold and defrost-window tuning, degree-minute accumulation, a local log that survives the internet, modelling of NJ's two-stage cooling rule, and someone contractually responsible for a false-alarm rate at 2am. That is integration, calibration and reliability work, not a chat subscription.

impact_estimate.range: $3,000-$18,000 per year of protected margin, plus 2-4 hours a week of manual temperature logging removed
impact_estimate.assumptions: No single dominant term; the range spans the three contributors. (a) Avoided loss: the avenue's working figure of $5,000-$20,000 of perishable inventory behind one walk-in/cooler (inference from inventory reasoning, not a sourced figure); assuming one failure event per 3 to 1 years avoided gives roughly $1,700-$6,700/yr. (b) Labour: 2-4 hrs/week of manual checks and log-filling at the NJ Stockers and Order Fillers median of $17.91/hr ($37,250/yr) - https://www.onetonline.org/link/localwages/53-7065.00?st=NJ - equals $1,860-$3,720/yr, and the wage floor keeps rising ($15.92/hr NJ minimum from 1 Jan 2026). (c) Shrink: improvement against the USDA 4.5% fresh meat/seafood and 9.7% fresh vegetable loss baselines rather than elimination. Excluded because unmeasured here: avoided inspection re-checks and any insurance benefit. This is an inference for a single independent store; no study measures this for a NJ independent grocer.

opportunities.pilot_scope: One site, 4 monitored units (deli case, walk-in cooler, freezer, prep/kitchen cooling station), 4-6 weeks: week 1 survey, install and a silent baseline with alarms suppressed so we learn the defrost and stocking rhythm; weeks 2-4 live alerting to two named contacts with a weekly review call; weeks 5-6 hand-off with an inspection-ready log export, a two-stage cooling report matched against N.J.A.C. 8:24-3.5(d)1, and a documented false-alarm rate. Success metric: 100% of excursions above 41 F lasting more than 30 minutes on a product-simulating probe detected and alerted to a named phone within 5 minutes, zero missed days of record over 4 consecutive weeks, and under 2 false alerts per unit per week.
walk_in_checks: Stand in the store and count the refrigerated units: deli/slicing cases, European dairy and farmer cheese case, smoked-fish/herring/caviar case, walk-in cooler, walk-in or reach-in freezer, bakery retarder/proofer, plus any staging fridge behind the pickup counter. The unit count drives the price.
Look for a clipboard or paper 'temperature log' on the walk-in door: gaps, one pen filling a week of columns at once, or identical numbers down a column are the classic tell.
Is there a probe thermometer at the prep line, or only a hanging dial thermometer on a hook? A dial in the case measures air, not product.

Kitchen cooling practice: after cooking prepared foods (stuffed cabbage, cooked meats, soups, gefilte fish), are pans spread thin on a rack or stacked deep, and does anyone write down the 135 F / 70 F / 41 F times? Deep-stacked pans are where the four-hour NJ cooling clock gets broken.

Door gaskets torn or doors that don't self-close; a walk-in propped open during a morning delivery; ice build-up on the freezer ceiling/floor or frost on the evaporator coil (defrost or door problem).
Cases loaded above the load line so airflow is blocked, or product stacked on the floor - both shorten the time to an excursion and make probe placement harder.

Any monitoring hardware at all: no probe, no gateway, no antenna. Also check where the Wi-Fi access point sits relative to the box - metal walk-ins kill Wi-Fi, which is exactly the installation work we charge for.

A refrigeration contractor sticker on the condensing unit with a recent service date. That is both a warm prospect (they just had a failure) and the person whose cooperation we need so our probe isn't treated as tampering.
Ask one open question at the deli counter or office: 'have you ever lost a case overnight?' The answer is the discovery conversation.

opportunities.title: Catering and holiday pre-order intake agent that drafts the menu, the quote and the kitchen ticket - with staff approving
opportunities.problem: Catering is ordered by phone and cannot be ordered online at all, and the whole seasonal pre-order line - 14 items with individual lead times and pickup-only flags, plus 'call the store for a custom date or large order' - routes to one phone number during stated store hours. Every enquiry is a verbal data-gathering exercise (occasion, headcount, date, platter mix, pickup or delivery, dietary constraints) done by whoever is free, in one of five languages the storefront advertises, while the same person is also covering the deli counter. Friday-to-Sunday specials, Thanksgiving and the December holiday window concentrate this into a few weeks, and enquiries that arrive after 8pm or before 9am have no channel that promises a response time.
evidence: Catering 'is ordered by phone, not through the website' - customers must call (732) 679-3100 to plan a menu or place a custom platter order: https://emporiumfoods.com/catering

The seasonal pre-order catalog is a separate 14-item list (stuffed suckling pig $395, stuffed whole goose $325, duck, whole baked sturgeon, gefilte fish) with lead times, some pickup-only, and an explicit instruction to call the store for a custom date or large order: https://emporiumfoods.com/pre-orders

Contact page pushes phone as 'fastest for same-day help' for urgent order changes, pickup questions and availability; the fallback is a web form with a topic dropdown (general, product, order help, delivery/pickup, catering, feedback) and no live chat widget: https://emporiumfoods.com/contact-us
Hours are 9:00am-8:00pm seven days with no stated after-hours phone coverage, so evening catering enquiries sit until the next morning: https://emporiumfoods.com/faq
The storefront runs in five languages (English, Russian, Polish, Ukrainian, German), so intake quality varies with which staff member picks up: https://emporiumfoods.com/

Delivery is rules-based - five distance zones with minimum carts of $110/$150/$225/$290/$350 and $20-$30 fees in zones 3-5 - so a quote cannot be produced without a ZIP check: https://emporiumfoods.com/delivery-areas
opportunities.agent_design: A multilingual intake agent that sits in front of the phone rather than replacing it. Triggers: a web form or conversational page hit on the catering and pre-order topics, an inbound email, an unanswered after-hours message, or a staff member pasting a call note in. The agent gathers occasion, headcount, date and pickup/delivery ZIP, walks the customer through the catering and platter menu with 2-3 suggested combinations, checks the customer's ZIP against the five delivery zones (fee and minimum cart applied from published rules), computes an itemized quote from a maintained price sheet plus lead-time and blocked-date rules, and flags any item that needs a custom date or a large-order review. It then writes a draft ticket into a staff 'catering inbox' - price, items, date, pickup slot, deposit note, customer contact - and a person approves, edits or rejects it with one click before anything is sent. Approved tickets print as a kitchen sheet and release the customer confirmation; a calendar view shows headcount-per-date so nobody over-promises the kitchen. Hard escalation to a human phone call: anything above a dollar threshold, all custom/whole-animal items, any delivery outside zone 2, and any allergen or dietary question the menu cannot answer. Systems touched: the storefront's pre-order/product data (already exposed read-only by the published MCP server), the delivery-zone rules, a price/lead-time sheet, and an outbound email/SMS channel; during the pilot no transaction is charged by the agent.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A chatbot subscription cannot read the kitchen's capacity calendar, apply five-zone delivery minimums, hold a maintainable price and lead-time table, produce an itemized quote that a customer treats as a commitment, or hand a printable kitchen ticket to the prep line. This is a quoting and dispatch workflow with money and production capacity attached, in five languages, and it needs an approval gate and an audit trail - integration and reliability work, not conversation.

impact_estimate.range: $300-$1,600 per month in recovered admin time plus incremental catering and pre-order jobs
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference, since no call volume is published. (a) Admin: 8-20 hours/month of intake, quoting and re-keying removed at the NJ Customer Service Representatives median of $22.95/hr ($47,740/yr) - https://www.onetonline.org/link/localwages/43-4051.00?st=NJ - equals $185-$460/month; Order Clerk work (SOC 43-4151, NJ median $46,270) is the closer task match if you prefer that rate. (b) Revenue: 1-3 additional catering or pre-order jobs per month at $100-$400 each, from faster first response and after-hours capture, equals $100-$1,200/month; the higher end assumes peak season. Excluded: any claim that the agent raises average platter size, and any labour headcount reduction - this replaces a bottleneck, not a person. Peak-weighted (Thanksgiving/December) the low end of this range is the realistic steady state and the high end the seasonal month.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks: weeks 1-2 build the price/lead-time sheet and the room-per-date calendar with staff, encode the five delivery zones, and get 10-12 platter templates approved; weeks 2-4 live on the two highest-volume languages (English and Russian, with Polish/Ukrainian/German queued) with every draft going to staff for approval, not straight to the customer. Deliverables: a working quote-to-kitchen-ticket flow, a capacity calendar, a measured baseline-vs-pilot comparison of minutes per enquiry (baseline captured from staff time in week 1), and a list of the top 10 questions the agent could not answer, which becomes both the next build phase and the menu-data fix list.

opportunities.title: Multilingual storefront and after-hours answer agent running on their own published MCP server
opportunities.problem: The customer-facing stack is modern - a custom multilingual storefront, five delivery zones, reorder and saved basket, weight-based items re-priced on actual packed weight with a temporary authorization buffer - but there is no chat, no after-hours channel, and the published answers contradict each other. The live /pages/delivery page still describes UPS shipping with two-day dispatch while the FAQ says the store does not ship groceries out of state. Five languages are advertised, but the only real-time channel is one phone line staffed 9-8. That combination produces exactly the questions an agent should absorb: what do you have in stock, do you deliver to my ZIP and what is the minimum, when is my pickup, why did my total change after packing, and does this ship.
evidence: No live chat widget on the contact page; phone is positioned as 'fastest for same-day help' and the only fallback is a web form with a topic dropdown and a required order reference: https://emporiumfoods.com/contact-us

The storefront publishes a public read-only MCP server ('emporium-foods-storefront', v2.0.0) with tools for product search, store hours, pickup slots, delivery ZIP checks, specials and pre-orders - the live data an answer agent needs is already exposed as agent-readable tools: https://emporiumfoods.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json

Contradiction between two live pages: /pages/delivery carries 'dispatched within 2 days ... shipped via UPS with tracking' boilerplate while the FAQ states the store does not ship groceries to other states: https://emporiumfoods.com/pages/delivery and https://emporiumfoods.com/faq

Weight-sold items are ordered with an estimated weight and re-priced on actual packed weight against a temporary authorization buffer, a reimbursement question that will recur on every deli, cheese and smoked-fish order: https://emporiumfoods.com/faq
Hours are 9:00am-8:00pm seven days with income-generating traffic running to closing and no stated after-hours coverage of any kind: https://emporiumfoods.com/faq
Five-language storefront (English, Russian, Polish, Ukrainian, German) with per-language routes, so a monolingual answer channel cannot cover the advertised audience: https://emporiumfoods.com/
opportunities.agent_design: A grounded answer agent in front of the storefront, with three channels: an on-site widget, an auto-draft for the existing contact form (so the form stops being a dead end after 8pm), and a post-purchase status reply. Tool calls go to the store's own MCP server for live product search, hours, pickup slots, ZIP delivery checks, specials and pre-orders; retrieval goes over the FAQ, delivery-areas, catering, pre-orders and policy pages plus the order record behind a scoped read-only lookup. Guardrails are explicit and written down: never promise out-of-state shipping, never quote a firm price for a weight-based item (state the estimated weight, the re-price rule and the authorization buffer), never invent a delivery fee or minimum outside the five published zones, never confirm allergen safety beyond what the menu states. Anything about refunds, weight disputes, damaged goods, catering or a complaint escalates into a staff queue with a summary and the order reference, and the customer gets a real expected response time. A weekly job diffs the live policy pages against the source-of-truth rules and emails a short fix list - which kills the stale UPS-shipping page and is a visible, sellable win in week one. Human approval points: every escalation, a weekly review of a sample of transcripts, and a monthly read of the questions the agent could not answer, which feeds the catalog and the FAQ rather than being ignored. Data handling: PII is read through scoped, redacted tool calls rather than stored; transcripts are treated as discoverable records with a stated retention period; the privacy notice covers this under the NJ Data Privacy Act (P.L. 2023, c.266, effective 15 Jan 2025) and the widget is built to WCAG so it doesn't add ADA exposure.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: The hard part is not the chat window, it is truth. The answers depend on live stock, live pickup slots, a per-ZIP delivery matrix and an order record; the store has five languages and an existing contradiction between two of its own pages, so a generic assistant that sounds confident will start promising UPS shipping and wrong delivery minimums within a day. Wiring to their MCP server, deciding which questions must never be answered by a model, keeping five languages consistent and giving staff a weekly gap report is integration and evaluation work.

impact_estimate.range: $450-$1,400 per month in deflected contact time, plus uncounted after-hours capture
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference - no contact volume, ticket log or review content is published (Yelp returned 403 and no chat transcript source exists). Assumes 60-150 inbound contacts per week (phone + form) for a single-store market with delivery and catering, 3-5 minutes of staff time each, and 30-50% self-service on the informational questions the agent is allowed to answer (availability, ZIP/delivery minimum, pickup timing, hours, policy). 4-12 hours/week at the NJ Customer Service Representatives median of $22.95/hr ($47,740/yr) - https://www.onetonline.org/link/localwages/43-4051.00?st=NJ - gives $460-$1,380/month; rounded down at the low end for contacts the agent mishandles. Directional support: a GenAI support assistant raised issues resolved per hour by 14% on average across 5,179 agents, with the largest gains for less-experienced staff (https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161), though that was a Fortune 500 software support desk, not an independent grocer. Excluded: any claim of basket-size or conversion lift - the e-commerce field evidence shows conversion gains, not larger carts, and none of it is from a NJ grocer.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks on two languages (English and Russian) and after-hours-heavy traffic first. Deliverables: connection to the live MCP server, a 100-question gold set written with staff and scored before launch, a written answer-policy sheet (what it must never say), an escalation queue with order-reference lookup, a weekly transcript review meeting, and the policy-conflict fix list generated from the /pages/delivery vs /faq contradiction. Success metric to agree in week 1: at least 90% agreement with the gold set, zero answers that contradict the FAQ on shipping, and a measurable drop in the share of contacts that end in 'call the store'.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (22/30): unusually specific, primary-source operational evidence - catering and custom dates are explicitly phone-only, seasonal pre-orders carry per-item lead times and 'room left' checks, there is no chat and no after-hours channel, and an active deli/prepared-food/smoked-fish/bakery operation sits under NJ's 41 F holding and two-stage cooling rules. Held back because no call volume, review content (Yelp 403), headcount or revenue is public, so every impact figure rests on inferred enquiry volume. Fit (18/20): three of the strongest capabilities map cleanly - A on catering intake, C on the answer layer, E on the cold chain - and the store already publishes a read-only MCP server for product and fulfillment data, which is a ready-made integration surface and a strong signal they will tolerate a real system rather than a chatbot. Ability to pay (12/20): single location since 1995 with a kitchen, bakery, deli and a five-zone delivery operation implies real revenue and a genuine margin at stake, but size is unverified (likely low tens of employees), ownership is unverified, and the NJ minimum wage at $15.92/hr plus a soft NJ labour market (unemployment 4.2%) weakens the pure labour-substitution case. Ease (11/15): a custom Laravel/Livewire stack with a documented MCP server and JSON-LD means low integration risk, and the cold-chain pilot installs into existing boxes with no POS dependency - but there is no published decision-maker (only 'Mark' and 'Lenny' for advertising, no titles) and a phone-centric owner-operator culture means buying will happen in person, not by email. Strategic (12/15): the cold-chain brief and the multilingual-specialty-grocery answer agent are both repeatable across Middlesex County delis, ethnic grocers and caterers, and an MCP-fronted storefront is a reusable pattern for every tech-forward independent in the county. The physical-operation preference is satisfied deliberately: the E opportunity is cold-chain monitoring, not cameras-as-theft-detection, because the deli/kitchen/smoked-fish footprint is visible from the store's own site while loss-prevention evidence for this business is absent and any security install would drag a licensed alarm contractor into the deal. Deductions: no measured shrink or contact-volume baseline exists for this store, so all three pilots should be priced as paid evaluations with a week-1 baseline rather than as promised savings.

best_evidence_signal: Catering and custom pre-orders are phone-only with a seasonal catalog that has lead times and per-item 'room left' checks - a priced, capacity-bound workflow running on one phone line during 9-8 store hours: https://emporiumfoods.com/catering
suggested_channel: phone - call (732) 679-3100 and ask for Mark or Lenny, the contacts the store itself publishes for in-store advertising business; then walk in mid-morning on a weekday (not Friday-Sunday, which is their specials crush) with a one-page cold-chain audit and the free win of their own contradictory shipping pages in hand
